newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan hull insurers won"t confirm decontrol report.
newsitem.headline: Japan hull insurers won"t confirm decontrol report.

text.p: The Japanese Hull Insurers Union refused to confirm a newspaper report on Tuesday that it would liberalise marine insurance policy premiums from April.
"We have not officially decided it (liberalisation) and cannot make comments at this stage," a union official said.
The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said in its Tuesday edition that non-life insurers would liberalise marine insurance policy premiums from April.
The newspaper said the move by the insurers was to cope with intensified competition in world markets and compete with foreign non-life insurers which offer cheaper premiums than Japanese firms.

The union official said that while Japan"s Anti-Monopoly Law has not been applied to marine insurance policy premiums, the premiums are scheduled to be liberalised by the end of March 1998 following a revision in the Insurance Business Law which took effect last April.
